title: Fill-roster collapse -- U1 (C-01, W-22): ladder/rungMode folds fineLadder, phaseFineLadder, perceptualRamp -- docs/3d-audit/lane-reports/W-22-24-W-18-plan.md
notes: U1 populates COLLAPSE.ladder in scripts/build-tone-laws.js (survivor 'ladder', descriptor key 'rungMode', 4 options: coarse->ladder [default], fine->fineLadder, finePhase->phaseFineLadder, perceptual->perceptualRamp). PICKER_IDS 48 -> 45; ALIASES 0 -> 3 entries. Also fixed a real gap the plan did not anticipate: 'ladder' is the shipped DEFAULT and is deliberately NOT a member of SCENE3D_TONE_LAWS.IDS (confirmed IDS.indexOf('ladder')===-1), so it can never appear in PICKER_IDS (derived from IDS) -- the build script's own integrity throws (every ALIASES[x].into in PICKER_IDS; every COLLAPSE option's `law` in IDS) would have thrown the moment C-01's ladder-survivor row was added. Added an explicit DEFAULT_LAW ('ladder') exception to both throws in scripts/build-tone-laws.js so a survivor that IS the shipped default is a legal target -- this is specific to C-01 (the ONLY cluster whose survivor is the default, not a roster id); U2-U8 never need it. This is a data-only change confined to scripts/build-tone-laws.js, within this unit's file scope.

byte_identity.unit_test_sweep: tests/unit/scene3d-tone-law-collapse.test.js's new U1 describe block asserts the same byte-identity (JSON.stringify(SurfaceFill.buildObject(...)) equality) for all 3 folded ids via Params.resolveToneLaw, both directly (toneLaw:'ladder', rungMode:'<mode>') and through normalizeStyle's migration shim (toneLaw:'<foldedId>' -> {toneLaw:'ladder', rungMode:'<mode>'}). reading_the_pass: Per the plan's inverted convention for this effort: a byte-identical before/after pair IS the pass, not the usual failure signal. Each pair is identical because the collapse is a resolver, not a rename or a re-implementation -- surface-fill.js's TONE_ALGO dispatch (untouched by this unit) still receives the exact same internal toneLaw string ('fineLadder', 'phaseFineLadder', 'perceptualRamp', or the bare 'ladder') it always did; Params.resolveToneLaw and the migration shim only change HOW a user/document reaches that string (survivor id + rungMode, instead of the folded id directly), never the string itself.

visual_inspection.torus__hatch__ladder__med__a: LOOKED at the webp directly (Read tool). A torus rendered as concentric meridian rulings, denser toward the near rim, with a dark diagonal band of skipped rungs across the lower-left/centre where the tone drops out -- the ladder coverage-rung look, unchanged from the pre-U1 gallery baseline (md5-identical).
visual_inspection.torus__hatch__fineLadder__med__a: LOOKED at directly. By eye, essentially indistinguishable from ladder above at this crop/zoom -- the same overall ruling layout and dark band, with a very slightly denser cluster of rulings near the rim (consistent with the plan's measured 76 -> 78 paths, a 2-path difference that does not read as a materially different picture). This independently confirms the audit's own C-01 finding ('by eye indistinguishable at plot scale on torus and sphere') rather than merely trusting it.
visual_inspection.torus__hatch__perceptualRamp__med__a: LOOKED at directly. Also visually close to ladder/fineLadder -- same ruling family and dark-band placement; the audit's own measured non-monotone ink numbers (705.1 -> 775.0 -> 713.1 -> 687.8 mm across the 4 options) are consistent with 'the same picture, different coverage-rung boundary' rather than a genuinely different mark, which is why this cluster ships as a labelled enum, not a slider (Phase 2/U10 is where a real continuous rungFineness replaces it).

monotonicity: NOT asserted, per the plan's explicit instruction for C-01. Measured ink on torus+hatch+med (from the plan, restated here, not re-measured pixel-by-pixel by this unit): ladder 705.1 -> fineLadder 775.0 -> phaseFineLadder 713.1 -> perceptualRamp 687.8 mm. Non-monotone. rungMode ships as a labelled enum (coarse/fine/finePhase/perceptual) for exactly this reason.
